title: The sphere's count needs resolution width Theta(sqrt n)
claim: The sphere's count needs resolution width Theta(sqrt n). Every resolution refutation of the not-all-equal formula of the octahedral knot sphere K_k (n = 4k^2 points) has width at least c*k - 1 for an absolute constant c > 0, and width O(k) suffices. Duplicator answers from label states whose vortex lies outside the density-bad set of the pebbles (points x with at least s/C pebbles within distance s for some s). By the exact window criterion, an obstruction to moving the vortex is a negative cycle of a sheet system on the pebbles; it closes into a walk of length at most a constant times its number of pebbles that separates the two positions or passes through the old one, so one of them is density-bad, and a Vitali covering bounds the bad set by O(pebbles^2) points.
failure_conditions: A pebbled colouring and vortex on which the sheet criterion and the solver disagree, or a feasible case whose realization is not a single-defect state at the vortex matching the pebbles.
An obstruction certificate violating L <= 3r - 6 + H, or one that neither separates the two positions nor passes through the old one.
A Spoiler with at most c*k pebbles that traps the vortex against the density strategy (the simulated game is an illustration only).
A gap in the hand proof: the window criterion, the winding bound for shortest segments, the isoperimetric lemma or the covering argument.
foundation_claim_scope: The octahedral knot spheres K_k for every k (by the proof); the window criterion and certificates checked for k = 4..7; the game simulated for k = 6, 8 with up to 12 pebbles.

validation.independence: Written by Claude in one session at the repository owner's request on 2026-11-07.
validation.status: the theorem by hand (window criterion, certificate length bound, density covering, Atserias-Dalmau); computational checks of the criterion, of the certificates and of a simulated game; no human or external review
validation.novelty: new as far as found for these formulas: resolution width bounds for grid formulas (Tseitin, mutilated chessboard, Sperner tree-like) use expansion or tiling games; the delta is a density argument for a height principle with a vortex, where obstructions are closed walks with at most a constant number of steps per pebble.
